title: PII: the risks and the benefits

slides.title: Facts that point at you
slides.text: Pim calls these facts PII: your full name, where you live, school, birthday, location, photos and voice. Each one points at one person: you.
slides.alt: Would you rather use a nickname nobody can trace to you, or your real first name so friends can find you?

slides.title: Sharing buys real things
slides.text: Sharing PII can buy real things: an account, a delivery at your door, or friends finding you. Posting your work can even bring kind, useful feedback.
slides.alt: A second online dilemma: posting your work brings feedback, and can also show more than you meant.

slides.title: Risk grows in combinations
slides.text: One fact alone is a small risk, but combined facts can map your whole day. The wider the audience that sees them, the more people can join the dots.
slides.alt: An online dilemma in Pro: make it public and be found, or keep it private and stay safe — a real tradeoff.

slides.title: Spot the harvest
slides.text: A fun quiz promises your secret nickname. Watch what its questions collect along the way.
steps: asks the street you live on
slides.alt: A fun quiz in costume: which dragon are you? It asks for a first pet, a street and a birth month to play.

slides.title: Fixing an overshare
slides.text: Some sharing can be undone: delete the post and ask the service to remove its copies. Some cannot, so tell a trusted adult fast, and in some places the law can help too.
slides.alt: Would you rather delete an old post you are embarrassed by, or leave it up and laugh about it?

words.means: personally identifiable information, facts that point at one person
to share a fact about someone, on purpose or by accident
to gather facts about people, often without them noticing
everyone who can see what you shared, now or later

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Would You Rather and choose the Online topic: play Online: share or keep. For one dilemma, name the price in PII and say if the benefit is worth it.
